solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Some avoid lectures, spend time doing nothing

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A student skips lectures and spends the day doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To idle is to loaf about, passing time without any useful activity, so the verb phrase is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Tot before a play

indicators.note: before says the first piece is placed ahead of the next one in this down answer

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits, a dram

explanation.surface: A small child goes to see a play, or a quick drink is taken before the show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler, but here it is a small shot of whisky.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a work for the stage, so a play is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Instrument played in large concert, I suspect

indicators.note: as an adjective suspect means dubious or not genuine, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at a big concert guesses which instrument is being played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' reads as a verb of guessing but signals an anagram of LARGE CONCERT I.
explanation.definitionFit: An electronic keyboard that imitates a pipe organ is one kind of musical instrument.

clue.text: Rebellious at university, elected members

parts.note: to be up is British usage for being in residence at university
a candidate who is elected is in
arms are limbs, members of the body

explanation.surface: Students and elected representatives are in revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Members' suggests elected representatives, but it means limbs.
explanation.definitionFit: To be up in arms is an idiom for being angry and ready to protest or revolt.

clue.text: Harmony or division close to boundary?

parts.note: a unit is a section or division, as in an army

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A question of whether a border brings peace or splits people apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Unity means a state of agreement and concord, which is what harmony describes.

clue.text: Repeat? Learned line removed

indicators.note: removed says the following letter is taken away from the word before

parts.note: a literate person is educated, learned

explanation.surface: A teacher asks a pupil to repeat, after a learned line has been cut from the script.
explanation.definitionFit: To iterate is to do or say something again, a verb synonym for repeat.

clue.text: Soon enough exhausted, pleasure-seeking

parts.note: all in is an informal phrase for worn out
good-time describes someone devoted to having fun, as in a good-time girl

explanation.surface: A worn-out partygoer will recover eventually.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means at the right moment, eventually, without hurrying.

clue.text: Dirt involving top player? Hot stuff!

indicators.note: involving means the first word wraps around the second

parts.note: mud is wet dirt
a star is a leading performer

explanation.surface: A tabloid scandal digging dirt on a leading sportsman.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow condiment is pungent and fiery, playfully called hot stuff.

clue.text: Appropriate number, jazz number

parts.note: to appropriate is to seize or take
five is a number

explanation.surface: Choosing the right song for a jazz set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Appropriate' looks like an adjective meaning suitable; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dave Brubeck Quartet's famous 1959 recording is a well-known jazz piece.

clue.text: Record of Hungarian composer broadcast

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the letters follow the sound

parts.note: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian composer and pianist

explanation.surface: A recording of a Liszt piece goes out on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A list is a written register or catalogue of items, a kind of record.

clue.text: China with crack, not worth considering

parts.note: china plate is rhyming slang for mate, so china means pal
to have a crack is to have a go, an attempt

explanation.surface: A cracked piece of porcelain is not worth bothering about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' suggests porcelain, but in Cockney rhyming slang (china plate = mate) it means a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Paltry means trivial or meagre, too small to merit attention.

clue.text: Protective guard in residence

definitions.meaning: a cushioning shield worn on the shin or knee, as in cricket
slang for one's flat or home

explanation.surface: Safety equipment kept at home.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a cushioned shield and, informally, a place where someone lives.

clue.text: A nun ordered a large yearbook

indicators.note: ordered means put in a new order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A nun orders a large yearbook for the convent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges A NUN to ANNU; then add A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A publication brought out once a year, such as a children's comic book collection, is called an annual.

clue.text: Novel and Biblical book don read, excited

parts.note: Daniel is a book of the Old Testament

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An Oxford don reads a novel and a book of the Bible with enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges DON READ to give DERONDA.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Deronda is George Eliot's last novel, published in 1876.

clue.text: Get rid of dreadful boils in a hospital

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something in a terrible state, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A patient wants rid of nasty boils while in hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' reads as describing the boils but is the anagram signal; 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To abolish is to do away with something formally, to eliminate it.

clue.text: Serving soldier in pub is only to be expected

indicators.note: in says the soldier is placed inside the pub word

parts.note: the local is British slang for one's nearest pub
GI is an American enlisted soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier on duty drinking in a pub is to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is your regular neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Something logical follows naturally from the circumstances, so it is what one would predict.

clue.text: Simple tune from couple dispensing with piano

indicators.note: dispensing with means doing without, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: a pair is a couple
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: A duet drops its pianist and becomes a plain melody.
explanation.definitionFit: An air is a melody, especially a simple song-like one.

clue.text: Very protracted farewell

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired
protracted means drawn out, long

explanation.surface: A goodbye that goes on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal way of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Heading for farm, more unusual cattle feed

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

parts.note: odder means stranger, more unusual

explanation.surface: Travelling to a farm with some unusual cattle feed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading for' looks like travelling towards; it means the head of 'farm'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fodder is dried food such as hay given to livestock.

clue.text: Natural ability shown by Labour's leader in the course of charity bazaar

indicators.note: in the course of means within, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: a fair is a fête or bazaar, often to raise money

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: The Labour leader shows a talent for working a charity sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Flair is an instinctive talent or aptitude for something.

clue.text: Duke giving support to English soldiers? Correct

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting piece sits underneath, so the duke goes at the bottom

parts.note: men are soldiers, the ranks

explanation.surface: A duke backing English troops, with a final verdict of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct a text by removing errors.

clue.text: Family joined by grand royal personage

indicators.note: joined by says the next piece is attached after the first

parts.note: kin are one's family
G is slang for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A family grows by marriage into royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: A king is a male monarch, a royal figure.

clue.text: Woodwind instrument popular in Bordeaux

indicators.note: in places the word for popular inside the wine

parts.note: claret is the British name for red Bordeaux wine
in means fashionable, popular

explanation.surface: A wind instrument that is popular in the French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bordeaux' seems to be the city; it is the wine, called claret in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The clarinet is a single-reed wind instrument, part of the woodwind family.

clue.text: One who wrote stories about boxer's trainer

parts.note: c is circa, about
a handler trains or manages a boxer, or a dog

explanation.surface: A writer of stories about a boxing coach.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler wrote crime fiction such as The Big Sleep.

clue.text: Little boy's donkey, lacking name

indicators.note: lacking means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: neddy is a British informal word for a donkey

explanation.surface: A small boy's pet donkey has no name.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet form of Edward, a boy's name used affectionately for a youngster.
